title: Charles Ponzi: The Promise That Named a Fraud
description:
In 1920 Charles Ponzi promised Boston investors a 50% profit in 45 days. He arrived in 1903 with $2.50; by late July 1920 he was taking in $250,000 a day. Covering the money would have needed 160 million postal reply coupons, and only about 27,000 existed. Investors lost about $20 million. Every fact is from the English Wikipedia article on Charles Ponzi; the photographs are public domain, from Wikimedia Commons. Would you have trusted a promise of 50% in 45 days? Tell us in the comments.
